welcome.heading: Welcome to {{appName}}
welcome.law: Since June 19, 2026, EU law (Directive 2023/2673, Article 11a) requires stores that sell to EU customers to offer a 2-step withdrawal function for every order. A returns policy alone isn't enough.
welcome.app: {{appName}} adds a withdrawal button to your order status page, a page in your online store, or both. It handles the 2-step confirmation and sends the required confirmation email. You can manage all requests in one place.
welcome.imageAlt: A customer withdrawing from an order

requirements.button: A clearly labeled withdrawal button that customers can easily find
requirements.twoStep: A 2-step process: customers submit their withdrawal, then confirm it
requirements.email: An automatic confirmation email that customers can keep

welcome.penalty: If the withdrawal function is missing or broken, the law extends the {{days}}-day withdrawal period. Customers then get 12 months and {{days}} days to withdraw from each affected order.

form.heading: Turn on your withdrawal form
form.body: Customers submit their withdrawal, then confirm it in a separate step, as EU law requires. The form comes with default legal wording. Customers get {{days}} to withdraw, starting from delivery.

faqs.intro: Answers to the {{count}} questions we're asked most often.

stillStuck.heading: Still have questions?
stillStuck.body: If you can't find your answer here, email us. Our team reads and answers every message.

what-it-does.question: What does the app do?
paragraphs: It gives your EU customers a compliant withdrawal form. It also gives you one place to manage the requests that come in.

Customers open the form from their order, select the items they want to withdraw from, and confirm. Each request appears on the Requests page with the order, items, reason, and refund deadline. The related emails are sent automatically.

where-form-appears.question: Where do customers see the withdrawal form?
paragraphs: The form can appear in 2 places, and you can use either one or both. Choose them in Settings:
bullets: Order status page: the page customers see after checkout, and again when they open the link in their order confirmation email.
Storefront page: a dedicated page in your theme, for customers who look for the form later.
where-form-appears.closing: Each place also needs its app block added once in the editor. The setup guide on Home shows whether each block is added and links you to the right editor.

form-not-showing.question: A customer says the form isn't showing. What should I check?
paragraphs: Check these in order. The most common causes are first:
bullets: The withdrawal form is turned off, or the place the customer is using isn't turned on in Settings.
The app block hasn't been added to that page in the editor yet.
The order's country isn't one of your eligible countries. Check whether you've selected all EU countries or only specific ones.
The withdrawal period for the order has already ended. See the question about the withdrawal deadline.
The order was canceled, or it already has a pending withdrawal request. Each order can only have 1 pending request.

deadline.question: How is the withdrawal deadline calculated?
paragraphs: Under EU law, the withdrawal period starts when the customer receives the items, not when they place the order. Customers can also withdraw anytime before the items arrive. The app works out the deadline like this:
bullets: Not fulfilled yet: the withdrawal period hasn't started, so the order is always eligible.
Delivered with a delivery date from the carrier: the period starts on that date and lasts for the number of days you set in Settings. Right now, that's {{withdrawalDays}}.
Shipped without a delivery date: the app uses the carrier's estimated delivery date. If there isn't one, it uses the ship date plus your estimated transit time.
deadline.closing: If an order ships in more than 1 package, the period starts when the last package arrives.

transit-days.question: What is the estimated transit time for?
paragraphs: Many carriers don't send a delivery date to Shopify. Without one, the app can't tell when the withdrawal period starts, so it uses the ship date plus the estimated transit time you set.

Set it to about how long your packages usually take to arrive. Right now, it's {{transitDays}}. If it's too short, a customer's withdrawal period can end early, so it's better to set a longer time if you're not sure.

countries-languages.question: Which countries and languages are supported?
paragraphs: All EU countries are eligible by default. If you only sell to some EU countries, select Specific countries in Settings and choose them.
The form is available in {{languageCount}} languages: {{languages}}. Customers automatically see the form in their own language.
English is the base language. If you leave a translated field blank, the form shows the English text for that field instead, so customers never see an empty label.

after-submit.question: What happens after a customer submits a request?
paragraphs: These 4 things happen, in this order:
bullets: The request is saved with the Pending status and appears on the Requests page.
The customer gets a confirmation email. It's always sent, because it's the legal proof of their withdrawal.
You get an email too, if the New request notification email is turned on.
Your automation settings run. For example, the app can hold fulfillment or tag the order.

automation.question: What do the automation settings do?
paragraphs: The settings depend on whether any items have shipped when the request arrives. Different actions are possible in each case.
bullets: Before the order ships: the app can hold fulfillment so nothing ships while you review the request. It can also cancel and refund the whole order right away, and tag the order.
After the order ships: the items are on the way or delivered, so fulfillment can't be held. The app can create a return in Shopify and tag the order.
automation.closing: Automation never makes decisions for you. You always approve, reject, and refund requests yourself.

emails.question: Which emails does the app send, and can I edit them?
paragraphs: The app sends {{emailCount}} emails, and you can edit all of them on the Notifications page:
bullets: Customer withdrawal confirmation: sent when a customer submits a request. This email is always on.
New request notification: sent to your store's contact email. You can turn it off.
Withdrawal approved: sent to the customer when you approve a request. You can review it first, or turn it off.
Withdrawal rejected: sent to the customer when you reject a request. You can review it first, or turn it off.
emails.closing: You can edit the subject and body of each email in every supported language. You can also add variables, like the order number, the customer's name, or the requested items. The preview shows your changes as you type.

approve-reject.question: How do I approve, reject, and refund a request?
paragraphs: Open the request from the Requests page. The request page shows the items the customer selected, their reason, the order's status in Shopify, and your notes.

Approve or reject the request from that page. This also releases any fulfillment hold. You can refund the requested items there too. If the order hasn't shipped yet, you can cancel and refund the whole order instead.

The refund deadline is shown at the top of the page. Under EU rules, you need to refund within {{refundDays}} of the withdrawal. The page shows how much time is left and flags the request if the deadline has passed.
